title: WHAT GOD REMOVES BEFORE HE RECEIVES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'He is to remove the crop and the feathers and throw them down east of the altar where the ashes are.'" - Lev 1:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is an unglamorous verse. The crop is the pouch in a bird's throat where undigested food collects — often unclean things the bird has scavenged. It is removed and thrown away, along with the feathers, before the offering goes on the fire.

Even the smallest, cheapest offering was not exempt from preparation. God took the poor man's pigeon seriously enough to specify how it should be handled.

There is a gentle picture here for the believer. When God receives us, He also begins removing things — not to reject us, but because what we have taken in from the world does not belong on the altar. Some of it we picked up without thinking, the way a bird swallows whatever it finds. Sanctification is God's patient work of separating what is genuinely us from what we merely absorbed.

Hebrews speaks of throwing off everything that hinders (Heb 12:1). Paul urges us to put off the old self (Eph 4:22). This is not God finding fault. It is God preparing what He has already accepted.

If God is currently pulling something out of your life, it is because He intends to receive you fully, not to send you away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I absorbed from the world that God may be gently removing?
2. Do I see God's correction as rejection, or as preparation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take out of me whatever does not belong on Your altar. I trust that Your removing hand is a loving one. Amen.
